cases.note: A DFARS clause with a four-digit suffix and no paragraph groups emits the part.section ancestor and the four-digit alias
Four paragraph groups drop one at a time from the right, followed by part.section and the four-digit alias 7002
Three paragraph groups with a one-digit suffix emit four ancestors down to 31.205 and no alias
CAS clauses with two-digit suffixes emit their ancestors down to part.section and no alias
A clause with three paragraph groups and no hyphen suffix drops one group at a time down to part.section
Among suffixes of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 digits, only the 4-digit suffix 1234 emits an alias
A suffix containing a letter does not match (-digits) in shape 9 and splits after 252.204, whereas 252.204-0000 emits 252.204 and 0000
Alphanumeric paragraph groups (1a) and (2b) are dropped right-to-left before emitting part.section and the four-digit alias
Bare part.section numbers with neither hyphen suffix nor paragraph group emit no extras
Every source version token on the index side is immediately followed by its unversioned source id
An unversioned source id after a source version stays in the stream; the index side keeps both s-0042 occurrences
Company versioned ids across multiple two-letter prefixes each emit their unversioned company id on the index side
A ten-digit company versioned id emits its ten-digit unversioned company id
Unversioned company ids and company claim ids emit no extras on the index side
Unversioned Corpus source, claim, question and conflict ids emit no extras on the index side
A multi-cite bracket containing a Corpus source version, a company versioned id and a clause locator emits extras for all three in order
When both a deep clause citation and an ancestor appear in the same indexed field, each emits its full ancestor chain without deduplication
Extras for 15.404-1(a) are emitted immediately before the lexer moves on to the overlong group 12345
An trailing unclosed parenthesis after (a) stops the match at 252.204-7012(a), which still emits its ancestors and 7012 alias
When a trailing letter causes shape 9 to fail the boundary check, shape 10 matches 252.204 and no clause extras are emitted
When a trailing letter causes shapes 1 and 7 to fail their boundary check, shapes 2 and 8 match the unversioned stem and v2x becomes a word
0.7012 has a four-digit fraction so shape 10 takes it with no extras; 3.141-7012 has a three-digit section and four-digit suffix so shape 9 emits 3.141 and 7012
A four-digit paragraph group without a hyphen suffix drops the group to emit 15.404 and does not emit 1000 as a suffix alias
A paragraph group happens to hold four digits on a four-digit suffix clause: the group is dropped first, then the suffix, then the suffix alias is emitted
Repeated company versioned ids on the index side repeat both the versioned token and the unversioned extra
